note.note:
History:
- Chief complaint: New severe “blinding” headache for 3 days, constant and impairing ability to work.
- Onset/course: Sudden on awakening 3 days ago; continuous since. Partial relief with ibuprofen but never resolves.
- Severity: Up to 8/10, improves to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.
- Location/quality: Diffuse; worse over right eye. Occasional brief stabbing pain when standing quickly; sensation of “something moving” with sudden head movement.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia; intermittent visual disturbance described as “shooting lights/weird vision”; mild nausea, no vomiting.
- Relevant negatives: No focal neurologic symptoms (no tingling, numbness, weakness); no change in smell/taste; no fever; no sore throat/ear pain/sinus pain; no cough or phlegm; no nosebleeds/hemoptysis; no weight change. Able to sleep; not woken from sleep but wakes with headache.
- Prior headaches: Intermittent, milder headaches previously that resolved within 1–2 days with ibuprofen; no prior episodes this severe or prolonged.
- Impact: Difficulty focusing; missed portions of work-from-home days.
- Other: Recent eye exam reportedly normal. No recent travel.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic conditions: None reported. Remote history of unspecified pain in youth (no cause found).
- Allergies: No known drug allergies.
- Medications: 
  - Combined oral contraceptive pill (exact product not documented), started ~1 year ago; no side effects reported.
  - Ibuprofen as needed for headache; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Family history: Mother has severe migraines with vomiting.
- Vitals/BP history: BP reportedly normal at pharmacy 1 year ago when starting pill.
- Social: Lives alone; works from home; non-smoker; alcohol about once weekly (“three” amount unspecified); no recreational drugs.

Physical Examination:
- Not recorded. (Teleconsultation; no vitals, neurologic exam, or fundoscopic exam performed.)

Impression:
- New-onset severe persistent headache with photophobia and positive visual phenomena, most consistent with migraine with aura; first significant episode warrants in-person neurologic and fundoscopic examination and BP check.
- DDx (consistent with transcript):
  - Migraine with aura/status migrainosus: Severe, persistent headache with photophobia and visual phenomena; family history supports.
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis: Consider given estrogen-containing OCP use and new persistent severe headache without full relief; no focal deficits reported.
  - Tension-type headache: Possible but less likely due to photophobia and visual symptoms.

Management Plan:
- Medication: Prescribed an anti-inflammatory agent “stronger than ibuprofen” to use instead of ibuprofen; dose/route/frequency not documented. Take with food.
- May take paracetamol concurrently; dose/frequency not documented.
- Arrange in-person appointment for:
  - Full neurologic examination.
  - Fundoscopic exam to assess back of the eyes.
  - Blood pressure measurement.
- Contraception: Continue current pill for now; if migraine with visual symptoms is confirmed, contraceptive method may need to be changed.
- Safety-netting: If headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes before the appointment, attend Emergency Department (A&E) or call the clinic for advice.
- If symptoms settle before the appointment, the visit can be canceled.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with 3 days of continuous, severe headache with photophobia and visual phenomena, partially relieved by ibuprofen. No focal neurologic deficits or systemic infection signs. Working diagnosis is migraine with aura; in-person exam and symptomatic therapy initiated, with safety-net advice and contraceptive review planned.

Key Takeaways:
- Start the prescribed anti-inflammatory with food; paracetamol can be taken at the same time.
- Book and attend the in-person visit for neurologic, eye, and blood pressure checks.
- Seek urgent care if the headache worsens, changes, or becomes intolerable.

Next Steps:
- Patient to schedule the in-person appointment with the support team.
- Begin prescribed medication as directed.
- Reassess after exam; consider changing contraceptive if migraine with aura is confirmed.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; full neurologic exam; fundoscopic findings; current BP; exact OCP name; medication names and dosing; pregnancy status and LMP; detailed alcohol quantity; formal ROS for neck stiffness/rash/fever confirmation.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some audio gaps/inaudible segments; OCP name and alcohol quantity incomplete.
